writeup: TIC 378367349 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 30.207391 days and a primary eclipse depth of 2.04 percent. A secondary eclipse was detected at 6.9 sigma significance, and the automated detection pipeline assigned a signal-to-noise ratio of 256.1. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, two important caveats apply: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the initially measured period was actually half the true orbital period, and the pixel-level analysis places the dimming source only 0.085 pixels closer to the target than to a nearby bright star - within TESS's systematic centroid uncertainty of 0.10 to 0.3 pixels. TESS's resolution cannot confidently rule out contamination from the neighbor star.
